probka.z_danych_cm: From {{p}} stitches per 10 cm and {{w}} cm.
probka.z_danych_in: From {{p}} stitches per 4 in and {{w}} in.
probka.blad_brak: Enter the stitches in your swatch first.
probka.kategoria: Category {{n}}, {{nazwa}}: {{min}}–{{max}} stitches per 4 in, knitted in stockinette stitch.
probka.kategoria_otwarta: Category {{n}}, {{nazwa}}: at most {{max}} stitches per 4 in, knitted in stockinette stitch.
probka.kategoria_obie: This gauge fits both category {{a}} and category {{b}}.
probka.kategoria_miedzy: This gauge falls between categories {{a}} and {{b}}.
probka.kategoria_powyzej: This gauge is above category 0, which goes up to {{max}} stitches per 4 in.
probka.uwaga_kategoria: Yarn weight categories are only a guide, not a list of yarns you can swap. Even with matching gauge, two yarns can feel and drape differently.
probka.uwaga_oczka: Block your swatch, then compare it with your pattern: patterns give gauge after blocking.
probka.uwaga_koronka: Lace yarn is hard to pin to a gauge range; always go by the gauge in your pattern.
probka.uwaga_zaokraglenie: Your gauge per 4 in is rounded to the nearest whole stitch.
probka.uwaga_4in: The standard way to give gauge is stitches and rows per 4 in/10 cm. 4 in is exactly 10.16 cm.

druty.uwaga_mm: Go by the size in millimeters: letter and number sizes vary from maker to maker.
